newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl ready to meet SPD on tax "day or night".
newsitem.headline: Kohl ready to meet SPD on tax "day or night".

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Tuesday he wanted to stay in touch with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) over tax reforms and added cross-party talks on the issue could resume at any time.
"We can talk to each other, day or night," Kohl told a meeting of regional officials of his Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party.

Talks between the two sides on government plans to axe 30 billion marks off Germans' tax bills collapsed in acrimony last week, but both sides are probing to see whether a new attempt to break a policy deadlock is possible.

Kohl added, however, that his government was pressing ahead with pushing its tax-cutting plans through parliament. The measures should clear the Bundestag lower house at an extra sitting which will be called during the summer recess.
He added he would then have to wait to see what the SPD-controlled Bundesrat, parliament's second chamber, does with the tax reforms.
Kohl also did not rule out a future meeting on tax with SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine: "I am always ready to meet Herr Lafontaine. I'm not afraid of contact."
